empirical_translation_rationale: Dalfampridine improves timed walking in a subset with demyelinating multiple sclerosis, but no evidence shows rescue in UNC80-deficient neurons and conduction biology is mismatched. Sources: DOI:10.1016/s0140-6736(09)60442-6
hypothesis_report: Dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine) is a broad potassium-channel blocker that can prolong axonal depolarization and enhance transmitter release, so reducing an opposing outward current could, in principle, compensate for deficient UNC80-dependent inward leak and increase soma-to-synapse propagation or motor output without repairing UNC80 or NALCN (DAILYMED:ed826777-b8c4-4d35-aa64-a4c28452baa8; DOI:10.1113/jphysiol.1982.sp014180). The disease bridge is directionally plausible but indirect: a patient variant and UNC80-null neurons show markedly reduced NALCN current, whereas C. elegans loss of the complex preserves somatic activity in some neurons while reducing presynaptic calcium events and neuromuscular transmission (DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.004; DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1371/journal.pbio.0060055). Positive empirical translation is limited to other pathologies: in a randomized multiple-sclerosis trial, sustained-release fampridine produced a timed-walk response in 35% versus 8% on placebo, demonstrating that systemic exposure can improve motor performance in a subset with demyelinating conduction failure but not that it corrects an UNC80 channelosome defect (DOI:10.1016/S0140-6736(09)60442-6). Material counterevidence narrows the hypothesis: 4-aminopyridine caused spontaneous or multiple firing in some demyelinated axons, and higher concentrations suppressed conduction, while the label warns of seizures (DOI:10.1016/0006-8993(86)90652-9; DOI:10.1016/s0306-4522(96)00477-0; DAILYMED:ed826777-b8c4-4d35-aa64-a4c28452baa8). Exposure and target interpretation are especially uncertain because cloned human Kv1.1, Kv1.2, and Kv1.4 channels in HEK293 cells had IC50 values of 242-399 µM, leaving unresolved which native neuronal potassium currents are engaged at a tolerable CNS exposure and whether such engagement is spatially selective enough to help deficient cells (DOI:10.3109/21556660.2013.791623). Whole-cell current reduction is also not universal across UNC80 alleles: a disease-associated truncation retained whole-cell NALCN current but lost dendritic localization and UNC79 recruitment, so assembly, trafficking, developmental wiring, or cell-type-specific conductance balance could be rate-limiting rivals that potassium blockade cannot repair (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8). Moreover, enhanced release at both excitatory and inhibitory synapses, repetitive firing, or isolated terminal release without restored soma-to-synapse coupling could mimic benefit or worsen circuit organization; the unresolved central-versus-peripheral basis of hypotonia further weakens direct transfer to muscle tone. No exact-disease dalfampridine or 4-aminopyridine use or testing was found in the packet corpus or a targeted PubMed title/abstract search. Viability therefore rests on a genotype-matched, patient-derived dose-response experiment measuring resting potential, paired somatic and presynaptic activity, transmitter output, and hyperexcitability in deficient and corrected neurons; selective restoration of temporally coupled propagation within a seizure-free exposure window would support compensation, whereas target engagement without rescue, tonic firing, depolarization block, or equal effects in corrected controls would favor the rival explanations.

name: teprenone
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: The Arg2842Gln-equivalent allele retains UNC80 expression yet directly shows markedly reduced UNC79 co-association, and UNC80-mediated UNC79 recruitment is proximal to NALCN-complex assembly; transfer to native human neurons and other alleles remains unresolved. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-30403-7
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Heat-shock amplification could improve an allele-specific UNC80 conformer and then UNC79 recruitment, but UNC80 is not established as an HSP-dependent client and teprenone can directly inhibit HSP70 or trigger HSP70-independent stress. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.12.031; DOI:10.1124/mol.107.039164
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug HSP70 binding, HSF1 release, and HSP induction are established, including human tissue pharmacodynamics, but the net chaperone action is context dependent and can include HSP70 inhibition and ER-stress toxicity. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.12.031; DOI:10.1016/j.hrthm.2019.07.010; DOI:10.1124/mol.107.039164
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Oral human systemic exposure and peripheral target engagement are documented, but neuronal exposure is unmeasured, rat-brain induction used a high dose, and exposure is strongly food dependent. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2005.11.065; PMID:6885198; DOI:10.1159/000106756
empirical_translation_rationale: No teprenone phenotype test exists in UNC80-deficient systems; the retained evidence establishes heat-shock responses in other tissues or species rather than rescue of binding, assembly, localization, or current. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2005.11.065; DOI:10.1016/j.hrthm.2019.07.010; DOI:10.1159/000106756
hypothesis_report: Teprenone (geranylgeranylacetone, GGA) is a scientifically usable but highly provisional pharmacological probe of whether increasing cellular heat-shock capacity can improve the Arg2842Gln UNC80 conformational ensemble: this allele-equivalent retains UNC80 expression yet recovers about 60% less UNC79 by co-immunoprecipitation, while UNC80 normally recruits UNC79 into the NALCN complex, so an input-normalized increase in variant UNC80-UNC79 association followed by increased NALCN-associated UNC79 would be directionally consistent with rescue of the focal binding defect and its propagation to channelosome assembly (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-30403-7). GGA directly binds the HSP70 C-terminal substrate-binding region, suppresses HSP70 chaperone activity in vitro, and releases HSF1, providing a mechanistic route to heat-shock-gene induction but also warning that the compound is not simply an HSP70 functional enhancer (DOI:10.1016/j.bbrc.2006.12.031); oral GGA increased rat-brain HSP70 (DOI:10.1016/j.neulet.2005.11.065), and translation beyond gastric tissue is supported by a small placebo-controlled cardiac-surgery study in which 400 mg/day for three days increased atrial HSPA1 and HSPB1, although total and phosphorylated HSF1, HSPD1, and HSPA5 were unchanged (DOI:10.1016/j.hrthm.2019.07.010), while 150 mg/day also increased human gastric-mucosal HSP70 (DOI:10.1159/000106756). These observations do not establish neuronal target engagement at clinically relevant exposure: brain induction used a much larger rodent dose, human brain concentrations are unreported, and in four patients food increased systemic AUC after 100 mg by 30- to 45-fold, indicating unusually strong administration-dependent exposure (PMID:6885198). The apparent positive endpoint could instead reflect increased UNC80 or UNC79 abundance, altered solubility or epitope accessibility, generalized stress, or co-immunoprecipitation artefact rather than restored affinity; moreover, at >=100 micromolar GGA induced GRP78, unfolded-protein-response signaling, and mesangial-cell apoptosis without increasing HSP70, establishing concentration- and cell-context-dependent HSP70-independent toxicity (DOI:10.1124/mol.107.039164). A decisive experiment therefore needs concentration and time courses in an Arg2842Gln human-neuronal model with total and soluble UNC80/UNC79, cytotoxicity, HSPA1 induction, input-normalized co-immunoprecipitation plus an orthogonal interaction assay, NALCN-associated UNC79, surface localization, and regulated current, alongside HSF1/HSPA1 perturbation to separate heat-shock dependence from direct HSP70 inhibition or other GGA actions; no prior teprenone use or testing in exact UNC80 deficiency was identified, and it remains unknown whether this variant is chaperone-responsive or whether improved binary association is sufficient for assembly and function.

name: levosimendan
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Hypotonia-associated secretion-clearance failure is reported in one UNC80 child, but the contribution of respiratory muscle contractile reserve versus central and bulbar lesions is unmeasured. Sources: DOI:10.7759/cureus.4395; DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.004
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Respiratory-muscle calcium sensitization could improve pressure from residual drive, but central drive, bulbar/glottic coordination, aspiration, and secretion load may remain limiting and stronger pressure need not improve cough flow. Sources: DOI:10.7759/cureus.4395; DOI:10.1164/rccm.200805-732oc
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug calcium sensitization increases submaximal force in human diaphragm fibers and acutely improves diaphragm neuromechanical efficiency, although maximal force is unchanged. Sources: DOI:10.1164/rccm.200805-732oc; DOI:10.1164/rccm.201107-1268oc
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human systemic exposure can engage diaphragm physiology, but a tolerated pediatric force-active exposure is undefined and hypotension and tachycardia constrain dosing. Sources: DOI:10.1164/rccm.201107-1268oc; DOI:10.1016/s1474-4422(21)00242-8
empirical_translation_rationale: Acute healthy-volunteer diaphragm effects did not translate to consistent benefit in ALS or mechanically ventilated adults, including a large phase III null for vital capacity and function. Sources: DOI:10.1164/rccm.201107-1268oc; DOI:10.1136/jnnp-2018-320288; DOI:10.1007/s00134-019-05767-y; DOI:10.1016/s1474-4422(21)00242-8
hypothesis_report: Levosimendan is a plausible distal, symptom-focused probe rather than a correction of UNC80–NALCN pathology: in skinned human diaphragm fibres it increased submaximal force by about 25% by increasing calcium sensitivity without increasing maximal force (PMID:18990676), and acute randomised testing in healthy adults improved diaphragm neuromechanical efficiency by 21% during inspiratory loading (PMID:21960535). An UNC80-deficient child was reported to require cough assistance because hypotonia prevented secretion clearance (DOI:10.7759/cureus.4395), while paediatric neuromuscular physiology supports reduced inspiratory volume and expiratory flow as contributors to ineffective cough (PMCID:PMC10928549); therefore, if residual neural and bulbar activation reaches respiratory myofibres, calcium sensitisation could increase pre-cough inflation or expiratory pressure. That directional bridge remains inferential because UNC80 loss primarily impairs neuronal channelosome function and motor output (PMCID:PMC4716670), and the limiting lesion could instead be central respiratory drive, soma-to-synapse propagation, glottic closure, bulbar discoordination or aspiration, airway obstruction or secretion load, or fixed deconditioning, so stronger diaphragm pressure need not improve expulsive flow. Translation is mixed and substantially negative: a small phase II ALS crossover trial missed its primary sitting slow-vital-capacity endpoint and produced only a post-hoc, period-adjusted supine signal (DOI:10.1136/jnnp-2018-320288); a randomised study in 39 mechanically ventilated adults found no improvement in diaphragm contractile efficiency (PMCID:PMC6773912); and the 496-participant phase III REFALS trial found no benefit in supine slow vital capacity at 12 weeks (difference 0.26 percentage points, 95% CI -2.03 to 2.55, p=0.83) or function and survival at 48 weeks, while increased heart rate occurred in 33% versus 7% and headache in 29% versus 22% (DOI:10.1016/S1474-4422(21)00242-8). The acute healthy-volunteer effect may therefore depend on preserved activation, task, route, exposure, or population rather than represent robust efficacy in chronic neuromuscular weakness; lack of blood–brain-barrier penetration is consistent with the intended peripheral action but precludes rescue of core neural drive, and no exact-disease levosimendan use or test was identified. A discriminating UNC80-deficiency experiment would pair transdiaphragmatic or maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressures with cough-flow waveform and peak cough flow at a haemodynamically tolerated exposure: increased pressure without improved cough flow would favour glottic or airway rivals, whereas no pressure change would argue against adequate muscle sensitisation or exposure in this setting.

name: Cilostazol
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Aspiration is established in UNC80 deficiency, but neither substance-P deficiency nor delayed swallow triggering is demonstrated and instrumental phenotyping is absent. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.013; DOI:10.1007/s00455-017-9832-0
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Raising substance P and shortening swallow-trigger latency could help a sensory-delay phenotype, but UNC80 aspiration has not been phase-localized and the route does not address several motor, residue, reflux, or cough mechanisms. Sources: DOI:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2008.01703.x; DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.013
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: PDE3 inhibition and cAMP elevation are established and exact-drug adult studies show substance-P and swallow-latency changes, but the mediating pathway is indirect and disease specific action is absent. Sources: DAILYMED:77e77eaf-5556-43ac-844e-c0e29f02fe07; DOI:10.1111/j.1532-5415.2008.01703.x
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Oral adult exposure reaches pharmacology, but pediatric exposure and safety for this purpose are unestablished and antiplatelet, cardiovascular, interaction, and heart-failure risks constrain translation. Sources: DAILYMED:77e77eaf-5556-43ac-844e-c0e29f02fe07
empirical_translation_rationale: Small stroke studies suggest latency or pneumonia benefit, but a large propensity-matched cohort found no advantage and slightly more aspiration-pneumonia readmissions, leaving clinical translation weak. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.jstrokecerebrovasdis.2012.06.008; DOI:10.1159/000531716
hypothesis_report: Cilostazol is an orally available PDE3 inhibitor whose established pharmacology raises cAMP while producing reversible antiplatelet and vasodilator effects [DAILYMED:77e77eaf-5556-43ac-844e-c0e29f02fe07]. In adults with prior stroke, a small randomized double-blind crossover comparison with aspirin reported increased airway and serum substance P and shorter latency of the evoked swallowing reflex [PMID:18554369]; a chronic cerebral-hypoperfusion rat study independently shortened elicited-swallow latency, increased swallow number, reduced lung bacterial colonies, and linked the effect to CREB phosphorylation, tyrosine-hydroxylase expression, and preservation of striatal substance P, although that model does not establish the same pathway in UNC80 deficiency [PMID:19032975]. Because recurrent aspiration is directly reported in biallelic UNC80 disease while the failing swallow phase remains unknown [DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.013], the directional bridge is testable but conditional: if delayed pharyngeal sensory triggering contributes materially, shortening trigger latency could narrow the interval for airway invasion, whereas oral-motor incoordination, inadequate laryngeal closure, post-swallow residue, reflux, impaired cough, secretion retention, or silent aspiration could dominate and would not necessarily improve. Translation beyond the latency assay is mixed and vulnerable to artefact: a 189-patient retrospective acute-stroke study observed pneumonia in 3/48 cilostazol recipients versus 24/141 nonrecipients [PMID:22877690], but treatment was not randomized and pneumonia is influenced by stroke severity, feeding route, recurrent stroke, and supportive care; conversely, a contemporary nationwide propensity-matched analysis of 65,125 pairs found more 90-day aspiration-pneumonia readmissions with cilostazol than with aspirin or clopidogrel (1.5% versus 1.2%), providing a material clinical null/negative result despite residual claims-data confounding and absence of instrumental swallow endpoints [PMID:37586338]. No cilostazol use, swallowing study, or aspiration-prevention trial in UNC80 deficiency was located, and neither substance-P deficiency nor delayed swallow triggering has been demonstrated in this disorder. Exposure is especially uncertain because the human swallowing and pneumonia evidence is in adults with acquired vascular disease, whereas many affected individuals are children; pediatric safety and effectiveness are unestablished, and the antiplatelet, tachycardic, hypotensive, interaction, and bleeding liabilities, together with the heart-failure contraindication, make direct physiological confirmation by swallow-provocation latency followed by videofluoroscopy essential before interpreting any event-level benefit [DAILYMED:77e77eaf-5556-43ac-844e-c0e29f02fe07].

name: salbutamol
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Hypotonia is universal and muscle wasting sometimes occurs, but evidence primarily supports neuronal and motor-circuit dysfunction rather than a primary, beta-2-responsive myopathy. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.004; DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.013; DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Beta-2 stimulation could increase force from residual neural drive, but central and synaptic dysfunction may dominate and hypertrophy or sprint power need not improve clinically relevant sustained or respiratory force. Sources: DOI:10.1038/ncomms7323; DOI:10.1371/journal.pbio.0060055; DOI:10.1111/sms.12298
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Exact-drug beta-2 pharmacology can alter strength, power, and muscle phenotype in humans, but force effects are inconsistent and causal separation from training, activation, and disease-specific transcript effects is incomplete. Sources: DOI:10.1042/cs0830615; DOI:10.1111/sms.12298; DOI:10.1152/japplphysiol.00553.2020
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Systemic oral exposures have produced muscle effects in humans, but force-active and tolerable pediatric exposure is unknown and supratherapeutic dosing impairs oxidative adaptation and raises cardiovascular concern. Sources: DOI:10.1042/cs0830615; DOI:10.1111/sms.70302
empirical_translation_rationale: Human healthy and athletic studies show heterogeneous muscle-group and sprint effects with null force/endurance findings, while SMA signals are confounded by SMN2 biology absent from UNC80 deficiency. Sources: DOI:10.1042/cs0830615; DOI:10.1111/sms.12298; DOI:10.1136/jmedgenet-2018-105482
hypothesis_report: Salbutamol is a beta-2-adrenoceptor agonist that would not repair the primary UNC80-NALCN channelosome defect but could provide a downstream compensation if reduced skeletal-muscle reserve materially amplifies generalized hypotonia: UNC80 case series establish persistent hypotonia and some weakness or wasting, while the available molecular and animal evidence points mainly to impaired neuronal excitability, sustained motor-circuit output, and synaptic transmission rather than a demonstrated primary myopathy (PMCID:PMC4716670; PMCID:PMC4716667; PMCID:PMC2265767). The directional bridge is therefore conditional—beta-2-adrenergic stimulation would need to increase force produced from residual neural drive, not merely muscle size. A small controlled study in healthy young men reported muscle-group-specific increases in quadriceps strength and inspiratory pressure, with no grip-strength or lean-mass change, supporting biological responsiveness but also showing heterogeneity (PMID:1335400). Material nulls weaken translation: in randomized elite athletes, 8 mg oral salbutamol improved short sprint peak power yet changed neither maximal voluntary contraction nor isometric endurance (PMID:25077918), and 11 weeks at 16 mg/day augmented type-IIa-fiber hypertrophy without additional muscle-force gain (PMID:33357007). These discrepancies leave learning, voluntary activation, glycolytic or sprint effects, training interaction, and measurement variability as rivals to a true increase in intrinsic contractile force; hypertrophy is specifically an unreliable surrogate. A one-year placebo-controlled study in adults with spinal muscular atrophy used 4 mg three times daily and reported molecular and exploratory motor signals (PMID:30593463), but its increase in full-length SMN2 provides a disease-specific rival mechanism absent from UNC80 deficiency, so it does not establish a general muscle-reserve effect. At a supratherapeutic 16 mg/day during resistance training, salbutamol increased lean-mass gain but impaired muscle oxidative markers and cardiopulmonary-fitness improvement and produced echocardiographic wall-thickness signals (PMID:42274909), indicating that an exposure sufficient for anabolism may trade against endurance or cardiovascular tolerability. No report or trial of salbutamol/albuterol in UNC80 deficiency was identified. Viability therefore turns on a blinded exposure-response experiment that separates motor-unit-normalized and electrically evoked limb and respiratory force from muscle cross-sectional area, spontaneous neural drive, fatigue, and training; hypertrophy without force, a response confined to supratherapeutic exposure, or no benefit in UNC80-relevant neuromuscular models would reject the proposed compensation, while the safe force-active exposure and the fraction of UNC80 disability attributable to muscle rather than central drive remain critical unknowns.

name: epothilone D
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: A disease-analogous UNC80 truncation directly causes somatic retention and absent neuritic localization while sparing whole-cell current, but this is allele-specific and demonstrated with tagged constructs in mouse neurons. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Greater microtubule capacity might redistribute truncated UNC80, but no microtubule deficit is shown and deletion of the cargo-localization/UNC79-binding region is a stronger bottleneck that track stabilization cannot replace. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1016/j.brainresbull.2022.10.008
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Epothilone D directly stabilizes tubulin, reaches mouse brain, changes acetylated tubulin, and alters axonal microtubules and transport, although architecture changes are not uniformly favorable. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.phrs.2010.12.002; DOI:10.1016/j.brainresbull.2022.10.008; DOI:10.1523/jneurosci.4922-11.2012
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Brain exposure and prolonged pharmacodynamics are shown in mice and very low intravenous doses entered a human Alzheimer trial, but no trial results define engagement and developing-neuron and oncology neurotoxicity narrow the window. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.phrs.2010.12.002; NCT01492374; DOI:10.1007/s10637-011-9765-7; DOI:10.1038/s41598-020-57718-z
empirical_translation_rationale: Axonal transport improved in a tauopathy mouse model, but no UNC80 redistribution or local NALCN physiology has been tested and neuronal toxicity complicates transfer. Sources: DOI:10.1523/jneurosci.4922-11.2012; DOI:10.1038/s41598-020-57718-z
hypothesis_report: Epothilone D is scientifically useful here principally as a discriminating transport-capacity probe, not as an established rescue: it binds luminal beta-tubulin and promotes polymerization (DOI:10.1016/j.brainresbull.2022.10.008), crosses the mouse blood-brain barrier, persists longer in brain than blood, and at 1 mg/kg increased brain acetylated tubulin seven days after dosing (DOI:10.1016/j.phrs.2010.12.002); in aged PS19 tau-transgenic mice, low-dose treatment increased axonal microtubule density and fast axonal transport while reducing axonal dystrophy (DOI:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.4922-11.2012). The proposed UNC80 bridge is directionally coherent only as an inference: L2654*-truncated UNC80 is retained in the soma and absent from axons and dendrites despite robust whole-cell NALCN current, so increasing usable microtubule polymer might raise its neurite-to-soma ratio without changing bulk current (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8). That bridge is nevertheless weak because no microtubule defect has been shown in UNC80 deficiency, the localization result comes from overexpressed tagged constructs in cultured mouse hippocampal neurons rather than endogenous patient neurons, and the truncation deletes the C-terminal localization region and UNC79-interaction interval; an irreplaceable cargo-recognition or complex-assembly defect is therefore a stronger rival explanation than insufficient track capacity. Moreover, epothilone D does not simply create longer, straighter tracks: super-resolution analysis in PC12 axon-like processes found increased microtubule density but decreased individual length and straightness (DOI:10.1016/j.brainresbull.2022.10.008), so target engagement alone cannot be assumed to improve UNC80 transport. Target engagement without UNC80 redistribution is the decisive mechanistic null, while redistribution without restored local dendritic NALCN physiology would leave disease relevance unresolved; any general axonal or behavioral benefit could instead reflect nonspecific cytoskeletal remodeling. Exposure is a major constraint because epothilone D reduced viability, growth, and complexity in immature cortical neurons and altered mitochondrial transport at sublethal exposures in mature cultures (DOI:10.1038/s41598-020-57718-z), while an adult oncology phase I study found dose-related reversible neurotoxicity and dose-limiting sensory neuropathy at much higher anticancer exposures that do not define a developmental-neurology window (DOI:10.1007/s10637-011-9765-7). A completed 40-participant mild-Alzheimer trial tested nine weekly intravenous doses of BMS-241027 at 0.003-0.03 mg/kg but posted no results (NCT01492374), and no exact-disease use or testing in UNC80 deficiency was identified. A credible experiment therefore requires disease-relevant neurons, pharmacodynamic confirmation, quantitative endogenous or equivalently validated truncated-UNC80 neurite-to-soma localization, local dendritic channelosome readouts, and a dose range that jointly excludes mitochondrial-transport and neurite-growth toxicity.

name: progesterone
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: UNC80 loss directly reduces but does not abolish NALCN current, and extra NALCN can increase residual current, establishing a proximal and potentially modifiable electrophysiologic process with allele-specific constraints. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Increasing NALCN expression could enlarge residual current in synthesis-competent alleles, but assembly, gating, and neuritic localization may remain limiting and progesterone regulation in CNS neurons is unestablished. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1152/ajpendo.00320.2019
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Progesterone receptor signaling and a NALCN-related current are supported in receptor-expressing myometrial cells, but the effect is estrogen-context dependent, protein was not significantly above vehicle, and neuronal channel off-targets confound action. Sources: DOI:10.1152/ajpendo.00320.2019; DOI:10.1016/j.mcn.2011.07.002
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Progesterone can enter mouse brain, but rapid degradation, route and region dependence, and unknown clinically attainable free concentrations at relevant human neurons leave target engagement materially uncertain. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.ejphar.2010.05.033
empirical_translation_rationale: No progesterone study tests a beneficial UNC80 or neuronal NALCN phenotype; retained evidence concerns myometrial expression/current and general neuronal receptor signaling. Sources: DOI:10.1152/ajpendo.00320.2019; DOI:10.1091/mbc.11.7.2283
hypothesis_report: Progesterone is a plausible mechanistic probe, rather than an established treatment, for testing whether increasing retained NALCN pore abundance can enlarge residual conductance in UNC80 deficiency. In the key human myometrial study, 100 nM progesterone acting through PRA or PRB increased NALCN mRNA in receptor-expressing cells and estrogen-plus-progesterone restored a Gd3+/NMDG-sensitive, NALCN-dominated current relative to estrogen alone; however, progesterone alone did not increase NALCN mRNA in the HM6ERMS2 model lacking induced receptor, estrogen-plus-progesterone produced NALCN mRNA similar to vehicle, and NALCN protein was not significantly above vehicle, making the signal partly reversal of estrogen repression rather than demonstrated suprabaseline surface-channel amplification (DOI:10.1152/ajpendo.00320.2019). A neuronal genomic bridge is biologically possible because 100 nM progesterone drove nuclear progesterone-receptor translocation and RU-486-sensitive gene induction in cultured dorsal-root-ganglion neurons (DOI:10.1091/mbc.11.7.2283), but this does not establish NALCN as a progesterone-receptor target in relevant CNS neurons. The disease-side premise is stronger but incomplete: UNC80-null mouse hippocampal neurons retain a small NALCN-dependent current and extra NALCN expression increased it, whereas a disease-analogous truncation preserved whole-cell current while losing UNC79 recruitment and dendritic localization, so additional pore could help some alleles yet fail when assembly, gating, or neurite delivery is limiting (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8). Exposure is conceivable because radiolabeled progesterone entered mouse brain after intravenous or intranasal delivery, but rapid degradation and route- and region-dependent kinetics leave human neuronal target engagement unknown (DOI:10.1016/j.ejphar.2010.05.033). Functional readouts would also be confounded at high exposure: 50 µM progesterone rapidly and reversibly inhibited voltage-gated sodium current by 47% and also inhibited potassium and GABA(A) currents in rat striatal neurons (DOI:10.1016/j.mcn.2011.07.002), while endocrine actions and neuroactive metabolites provide further rival explanations. No exact-disease use or testing was identified. The decisive experiment is an allele-stratified panel of patient-derived CNS neurons exposed at clinically attainable free concentrations, with progesterone-receptor blockade or knockdown and measurements of NALCN RNA, total and surface protein, subcellular localization, NALCN-specific current, resting potential, and synaptic output; failure of receptor-dependent surface-current gain despite RNA induction would identify assembly or trafficking as the bottleneck, whereas any electrical improvement must be separated from acute off-target channel effects.

name: tauroursodeoxycholic acid
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: The focal missense allele directly weakens UNC80-UNC79 association while retaining protein expression and has a structurally plausible local packing defect, though native-neuronal consequences remain unmeasured. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-30403-7
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: A broad chemical chaperone could improve an altered UNC80 conformer, but misfolding or aggregation is not established and PERK, anti-apoptotic, or bile-acid signaling could mimic effects. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-30403-7; DOI:10.1038/s41598-017-03940-1
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: TUDCA has exact-drug anti-aggregation effects, but they occur in generic systems at high millimolar concentrations and causal separation from broader stress signaling is absent. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.abb.2014.12.031; DOI:10.1038/s41598-017-03940-1
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Oral human tolerability is documented, but neuronal free exposure is unknown and may be far below millimolar experimental concentrations; rat brain detection followed 400 mg/kg intravenous dosing during ischemia. Sources: DOI:10.1111/ene.12664; DOI:10.1097/00004647-200204000-00010
empirical_translation_rationale: No UNC80 or channelosome phenotype has been tested; retained positive evidence is generic anti-aggregation activity in stressed proteins and cells. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.abb.2014.12.031; DOI:10.1038/s41598-017-03940-1
hypothesis_report: Tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA) is a defensible chemical-chaperone probe, rather than an established therapy, for the specific possibility that UNC80 Arg2842Gln creates a recoverable C-terminal conformer: the mouse-equivalent Arg2910Gln construct retained total expression but recovered about 60% less UNC79 by co-immunoprecipitation, while the intact-complex structure places Arg2910 in an intramolecular UNC80 Arg2910–Glu2965 contact, making an indirect packing defect plausible but not demonstrating misfolding, aggregation, or a direct UNC79-interface lesion (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41467-022-30403-7). TUDCA reduced stress-induced aggregation and hydrophobic-probe binding in generic proteins, and a follow-up study again found anti-aggregation activity, but these experiments used stressed BSA and HepG2 cells and concentrations extending to 5–10 mM, so they do not establish native-state rescue of the very large cytosolic UNC80 scaffold and also leave PERK activation, anti-apoptotic signalling, altered degradation, or nonspecific bile-salt effects as rival explanations (DOI:10.1016/j.abb.2014.12.031; DOI:10.1038/s41598-017-03940-1). The decisive experiment is therefore a matched concentration-response study of wild-type and Arg2910Gln/Arg2842Gln UNC80, requiring an increased mutant-to-wild-type UNC79 co-immunoprecipitation ratio with unchanged soluble input UNC80, no increase in insoluble UNC80, and no change in UNC79 abundance, followed only then by NALCN-associated UNC79 and channel-complex readouts; parallel vehicle, wild-type, unrelated missense, lysis/pull-down, viability, and aggregation controls are needed because altered expression, survival, solubility, or assay recovery could mimic stronger binding. Systemic translation is uncertain: a rat stroke study detected brain bile acid after 400 mg/kg intravenous TUDCA but only in an ischemia-reperfusion setting and at low measured brain abundance, whereas oral 2 g/day was tolerable for 54 weeks in a small ALS trial without showing that neuronal free TUDCA reaches the millimolar concentrations used in aggregation assays (DOI:10.1097/00004647-200204000-00010; DOI:10.1111/ene.12664). No direct TUDCA experiment or prior use in UNC80 deficiency, no Arg2842Gln patient-neuron study, and no evidence that improving this binary association restores channel localization or current were found; a null binding result under exposure-confirmed, non-toxic conditions would favor a specific interface/packing defect that broad anti-aggregation action cannot rescue.

name: ricolinostat
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: A disease-analogous C-terminal truncation directly causes somatic retention and loss of UNC79 recruitment while sparing whole-cell current, making local trafficking material but allele-specific and mechanistically entangled. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Increasing tubulin acetylation and motor transport cannot necessarily replace the UNC80 C-terminal localization information or lost UNC79 recruitment, and no HDAC6 or tubulin defect is shown in UNC80 neurons. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8; DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Ricolinostat directly and structurally inhibits HDAC6 and increases acetylated tubulin in humans, although higher exposure begins class-I HDAC engagement. Sources: DOI:10.1073/pnas.1718823114; DOI:10.1158/1078-0432.ccr-16-2526
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human systemic engagement is peripheral, while mouse data directly show poor brain penetration and failure in a CNS phenotype at a peripherally active schedule. Sources: DOI:10.1158/1078-0432.ccr-16-2526; DOI:10.1186/s40478-018-0604-3
empirical_translation_rationale: Transport rescue is shown only in stressed non-UNC80 neurons, while poor brain penetration prevented cognitive rescue in a mouse model; no UNC80 localization phenotype has been tested. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7; DOI:10.1186/s40478-018-0604-3
hypothesis_report: Ricolinostat (ACY-1215) directly inhibits HDAC6, with crystallography showing active-site binding and a selectivity contribution from its bulky capping group (DOI:10.1073/pnas.1718823114); oral dosing in people produced systemic exposure and increased acetylated tubulin in peripheral lymphocytes, although higher exposure also began to affect the class-I-HDAC marker acetylated histone (DOI:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-16-2526). In stressed primary cortical neurons, ACY-1215 prevented tubulin deacetylation and HDAC6 inhibitors restored BDNF transport velocity, supporting the proposed direction of increasing microtubule-dependent cargo transport (DOI:10.1038/s41419-019-1920-7). The disease-side observation is nevertheless different: UNC80 L2654* is retained in the soma because truncation removes a mapped C-terminal localization function, while the same protein retains NALCN association and robust whole-cell leak current but loses UNC79 recruitment (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8). Thus, increasing microtubule motor engagement could raise the neurite-to-soma ratio only if truncated UNC80 still loads onto a competent motor-adaptor pathway; neither that loading nor disease-associated tubulin hypoacetylation or HDAC6 overactivity has been demonstrated, and greater track capacity cannot necessarily replace deleted cargo-localization information. The gp120 experiment is an injury model rather than an UNC80-cargo experiment, so its transport rescue could reflect reversal of stress-induced cytoskeletal damage, and HDAC6 inhibition also changes non-tubulin substrates. Exposure is a material negative: ricolinostat poorly penetrated mouse brain and failed to reverse a cisplatin-induced cognitive deficit at a schedule that was active in peripheral neuropathy, whereas a brain-penetrant HDAC6 inhibitor was effective (DOI:10.1186/s40478-018-0604-3). No exact-disease use or test was identified. A discriminating experiment would establish acetylated-tubulin target engagement in UNC80-mutant patient-derived neurons, quantify endogenous UNC80 and NALCN-complex localization in neurites versus soma, and then measure dendritic NALCN-dependent physiology; unchanged localization despite target engagement would falsify the transport-capacity bridge, whereas redistribution without physiological rescue would favor the rival UNC79-assembly or local-channel-regulation lesion.

name: carbachol
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Residual NALCN current persists after UNC80 loss and in a disease-analogous truncation, supporting a proximal modifiable conductance in some alleles despite compartmental defects. Sources: DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Muscarinic drive might amplify residual somatic NALCN current, but the coupling may require intact scaffold components and cannot restore lost neuritic localization or assembly. Sources: DOI:10.1038/embor.2009.125; DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Carbachol evokes M3-associated sodium current reduced by NALCN knockdown in some systems, but it is indirect, used at high concentration, and contradicted by a heterologous null replication. Sources: DOI:10.1038/embor.2009.125; DOI:10.1111/bph.15104; DOI:10.1016/j.biopen.2018.01.001
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Systemic carbachol does not cross an intact rat blood-brain barrier and the marketed formulation is intraocular, leaving no established usable central exposure and broad peripheral cholinergic liabilities. Sources: DOI:10.1016/0024-3205(89)90289-0; DAILYMED:f28d7a56-e079-4a8b-ad81-9a97c780de67
empirical_translation_rationale: No UNC80 or disease-relevant beneficial phenotype exists, and the heterologous current failed a material replication owing to endogenous TRP conductance or seal artefact. Sources: DOI:10.1016/j.biopen.2018.01.001
hypothesis_report: Carbachol is scientifically plausible only as a discriminating probe of residual channel function, not as a repair of the UNC80-UNC79 scaffold: 100 micromolar carbachol evoked an M3-receptor-associated inward current in NALCN/M3R reconstitution, and a later HEK293T study found the response to be sodium-carrying and reduced by NALCN knockdown (DOI:10.1038/embor.2009.125; DOI:10.1111/bph.15104). The desired direction is relevant because UNC80-null mouse hippocampal neurons retained a small NALCN-dependent current, while a disease-analogous C-terminal truncation preserved whole-cell current despite losing UNC79 recruitment and neuritic localization, so some alleles could retain pores whose somatic current can be amplified (DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-17105-8). That bridge remains an inference: the positive carbachol data came from pancreatic MIN6 cells and heterologous systems, carbachol activates cholinergic receptors rather than binding NALCN directly, and neither the requirement for intact UNC80/UNC79 nor M3R-NALCN coupling has been tested in UNC80-deficient human neurons. A material null replication found muscarinic-agonist currents of similar frequency and amplitude in untransfected, M3R-expressing, and M3R/NALCN/UNC80/Src-expressing HEK293 cells, raising endogenous TRP conductance and weak membrane-glass seals as rival explanations for heterologous currents (DOI:10.1016/j.biopen.2018.01.001); even a genuine whole-cell response could remain spatially irrelevant where neuritic channel localization is lost. Translation is additionally constrained by exposure and selectivity: systemic carbachol behaved as a drug that did not cross an intact rat blood-brain barrier and changed behaviour only after focal barrier opening (DOI:10.1016/0024-3205(89)90289-0), while the marketed product is intraocular and its label records systemic parasympathomimetic adverse effects and no established paediatric safety (DAILYMED:f28d7a56-e079-4a8b-ad81-9a97c780de67). No exact-disease use or testing was identified. The critical experiment is therefore an allele-stratified carbachol concentration-response in patient-derived neurons with M3 blockade, NALCN knockdown or knockout, matched unedited controls, and compartment-resolved current and localization measurements; failure of a NALCN-specific response would favour loss of coupling, surface delivery, or neuritic localization over insufficient agonist drive.

name: lithium carbonate
disease_mechanism_validity_rationale: Postnatal head-growth deceleration is variably observed, but it does not establish a neural precursor or tissue-accrual deficit and is confounded by skull and systemic growth. Sources: DOI:10.1007/s00439-018-1929-5; DOI:10.1016/j.ajhg.2015.11.004; DOI:10.1002/ajmg.a.37929
directional_rescue_logic_rationale: Increasing precursor proliferation could improve tissue accrual only if an unshown proliferation deficit causes microcephaly; region-specific GSK-3 inhibition can instead suppress cerebellar progenitors. Sources: DOI:10.1186/2045-3701-1-18; DOI:10.1242/dev.177550
exact_drug_pharmacology_rationale: Lithium directly increases proliferation through GSK-3beta/NF-AT signaling at 3 mM in several rodent precursor preparations, but lower-dose findings and regional biology are inconsistent. Sources: DOI:10.1186/2045-3701-1-18; DOI:10.1006/cbir.1996.0101; DOI:10.1242/dev.177550
exposure_feasibility_rationale: Human brain lithium reaches about 0.52-0.87 mEq/L, well below the 3 mM proliferative condition, while labeled toxicity begins close to the therapeutic serum range. Sources: PMCID:PMC8332749; DAILYMED:57faf0b0-4380-4bbf-8de7-c3f9d74fc410
empirical_translation_rationale: No relevant beneficial phenotype exists in UNC80 models; the focal proliferation result is rodent culture at supratherapeutic concentration and another precursor line was null at lower concentrations. Sources: DOI:10.1186/2045-3701-1-18; DOI:10.1006/cbir.1996.0101
hypothesis_report: Lithium carbonate is a systemically deliverable source of Li+ that reaches human brain, with 0.52–0.87 mEq/L measured in ten lithium-carbonate-treated adults (PMCID:PMC8332749), but its proposed use here is a contingent phenotypic perturbation rather than a correction of the UNC80–NALCN channel defect. The positive basis is that 3 mM LiCl increased cell number and proliferation, but not survival, in a rodent neural-precursor line and primary rat and mouse precursors, with LiCl-versus-NaCl controls and pharmacological experiments implicating inhibitory GSK-3β phosphorylation and NF-AT activation (PMCID:PMC3125208). The directional bridge nevertheless assumes a lesion not yet shown in UNC80 deficiency: postnatal head-growth deceleration and microcephaly occur only in a subset, MRI is often structurally normal, and generalized short stature and low BMI make deficient brain-tissue accrual, skull growth, tissue loss, and systemic growth restriction live rival explanations (PMCID:PMC4716670; PMCID:PMC6671679; PMCID:PMC5671762). Translation is further limited because the proliferative experiment used LiCl at 3 mM rather than oral lithium carbonate at observed human brain exposure, a different murine neural-precursor line showed no growth difference at 0.1–1 mM Li2CO3 (PMID:9032938), and GSK-3 loss or inhibition suppresses SHH-driven postnatal cerebellar granule-neuron progenitor proliferation (PMCID:PMC6826032), making cell identity, region, developmental timing, and concentration plausible determinants of null or harmful effects. Exposure cannot simply be raised to reproduce the 3 mM culture result because the labelled toxic threshold of at least 1.5 mEq/L lies close to the 0.8–1.2 mEq/L therapeutic range (DAILYMED:57faf0b0-4380-4bbf-8de7-c3f9d74fc410). No published use or testing of lithium in UNC80 deficiency was located. The hypothesis is therefore testable only after an UNC80-deficient patient-derived progenitor or region-resolved organoid model demonstrates a baseline proliferation or tissue-accrual deficit; concentration-response studies should jointly measure EdU or BrdU incorporation, Ki-67, apoptosis, lineage output, organoid volume, cerebellar versus non-cerebellar effects, neuronal maturation and circuit function, and NALCN-dependent electrophysiology, with a null at clinically plausible brain concentrations, loss of appropriate differentiation or maturation, regional overgrowth, or a cerebellar decrement rejecting the proposed rescue.
